title: Early Warning Race - P Wave Versus Alert
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: A P wave, an S wave and a radio alert race outward from one rupture while four cities accumulate warning time, with the blind zone drawn as a shaded circle that grows and shrinks with the system's processing delay.

educational.topic: Early Warning Race - P Wave Versus Alert
learningObjectives: Assess how much warning time a city receives from an earthquake early warning system.
Justify why a blind zone exists near the epicentre that no system can eliminate.
Explain why early warning is not prediction.
Judge whether a given number of seconds of warning is useful.
prerequisites: Chapter 11: P and S waves and their speeds
Chapter 5: trilateration, for how a network locates an epicentre

keyQuestions: If the alert arrives before the shaking, has the earthquake happened yet?
Why does the city closest to the epicentre get the least warning?
What can actually be done in three seconds, and in fifty?
How does putting accelerometers in ordinary phones shrink the blind zone?
commonMisconceptions: Early warning predicts earthquakes before they happen.
A better system could warn everybody, including people at the epicentre.
The alert travels as a seismic wave.
A few seconds of warning is not worth having.
assessmentOpportunities: Computes warning time as S wave arrival minus alert time for a named city.
Records how the blind zone radius responds to the processing delay.
Argues, using the action lines, whether a given warning time is useful.
